q: A team wants to check whether the labels in a raw loan-history CSV already favor one gender, before any model is trained. Which tool and metric family fits?

options.A: SageMaker Clarify post-training metric disparate impact
options.B: Amazon A2I with a private workforce
options.C: SageMaker Clarify pre-training metrics such as DPL
options.D: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock denied topics

why: No model exists yet, so only dataset-level (pre-training) metrics apply. Difference in proportions of labels (DPL) compares positive-label rates across groups in the data.

others.t: Disparate impact is a post-training metric that needs a trained model's predictions.
A2I routes individual low-confidence predictions to human reviewers; it does not measure dataset bias.
Guardrails filters live foundation-model input and output; it does not analyze a training dataset.

q: A credit model never uses race as a feature, yet it denies one racial group more often. Investigation shows ZIP code acts as a stand-in for race. Which bias type is this, and what is the direct fix?

options.A: Historical bias; retrain on more recent data samples
options.B: Measurement bias; drop or transform the proxy feature
options.C: Sampling bias; collect a larger random sample of applicants
options.D: Aggregation bias; train a separate model per ZIP code

why: A feature that correlates with a protected characteristic is a proxy, which is measurement bias. Removing or transforming that feature addresses it directly.

others.t: Historical bias reflects an inequitable real world; newer data does not remove a proxy feature.
Sampling bias is about the data not representing the population; the stem names a proxy feature instead.
Aggregation bias is one model applied to groups needing distinct treatment, and splitting by ZIP would keep the proxy.

topic: Model Card vs AI Service Card
q: A compliance officer needs to understand the intended uses and limitations of Amazon Rekognition, an AWS-managed service, before approving it. Where should the team look first?

options.A: Run SageMaker Clarify against the Rekognition service
options.B: Create a new SageMaker Model Card for Rekognition
options.C: Read the AWS AI Service Card for Rekognition
options.D: Configure a Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock policy

why: AI Service Cards are published by AWS to document its managed AI services, and customers read them.

others.t: Clarify analyzes datasets and models you train; you cannot point it at an AWS-managed service's internals.
Model Cards document a model you built yourself, not an AWS-managed service.
Guardrails filters Bedrock foundation-model traffic and does not document a service.

q: A claims-processing model sends predictions below 85% confidence to human reviewers using Amazon A2I. Later the team edits the routing code to use 90% but forgets the A2I flow definition. What is the risk?

options.A: Human loops trigger at a threshold different from the routing code
options.B: Clarify will block the endpoint until the two thresholds match again
options.C: A2I will automatically switch the review work to a public workforce
options.D: The worker task template will fail to render for the reviewers

why: The flow definition holds the activation condition, and it should use the same threshold as the routing logic. If they drift, the human loop fires at different confidence levels than intended.

others.t: Clarify does not govern A2I routing or block endpoints.
Workforce type is configured separately; a threshold mismatch does not change it.
The task template defines the reviewer UI and is unrelated to the activation condition.

q: A hospital uses Amazon A2I to review model predictions whose review screens show patient health records. Which workforce choice is appropriate?

options.A: A public workforce with Guardrails word filters
options.B: A private workforce managed through Amazon Cognito
options.C: Public Amazon Mechanical Turk workforce for lowest cost
options.D: No workforce, since A2I only supports automated review

why: Review tasks that expose regulated data such as PHI need a private workforce, set up through Amazon Cognito.

others.t: Word filters belong to Bedrock Guardrails and do not make a public workforce safe for PHI.
Mechanical Turk is a public crowd and is not suitable when regulated data is shown.
A2I exists to add human review; automated-only is the opposite of its purpose.

q: A bank needs an explanation for every credit decision, and each decision must return in a few milliseconds. The explanation must reflect the model's actual decision logic. Which approach fits?

options.A: A larger foundation model behind Guardrails content filters
options.B: A natively interpretable model such as logistic regression
options.C: A deep ensemble with synchronous SHAP on every request
options.D: A deep neural network with a detailed Model Card attached

why: A natively interpretable model's logic is the explanation, so it adds no inference compute and reflects actual logic. Post-hoc SHAP is an approximation and adds per-request cost.

others.t: Guardrails filters content safety; it provides no per-decision explanation.
SHAP is an approximation, not actual decision logic, and adds latency when run per request.
A Model Card documents a model overall but does not explain individual decisions.

q: Which scenario describes TRANSPARENCY rather than explainability?

options.A: Publishing documentation on how the system was built
options.B: Telling a customer why their specific claim was denied
options.C: Computing SHAP values for one individual prediction
options.D: Showing which features pushed one applicant's score down

why: Transparency is about documenting the whole system: how it was built, trained and what it cannot do. Explaining one prediction is explainability.

others.t: Explaining one specific decision to a customer is explainability.
SHAP values for a single prediction are explainability.
Feature influence on one score is per-prediction explainability.

q: A Bedrock RAG assistant sometimes adds claims that are not in the retrieved policy documents. Which Guardrails capability directly targets this?

options.A: Word filters with a custom blocklist
options.B: Sensitive information filters
options.C: Contextual grounding checks
options.D: Denied topics for off-limits subjects

why: Contextual grounding checks verify a response is supported by the source content, reducing hallucination.

others.t: Word filters block specific words or phrases, not ungrounded statements.
Sensitive information filters handle PII, not factual grounding.
Denied topics block subjects the model should not discuss, not unsupported claims.

q: A company wants its Bedrock chatbot to never output the name of a specific competitor, but it may discuss the competing industry in general. Which Guardrails feature is the narrowest fit?

options.A: Content filters set to high
options.B: Word filters
options.C: Denied topics for the whole industry
options.D: Contextual grounding checks

why: Word filters block specific words or phrases such as competitor names, without blocking a whole subject.

others.t: Content filters cover harmful categories like hate or violence, not competitor names.
A denied topic would block discussion of the whole industry, which is more than required.
Grounding checks compare answers to source text; they do not block names.

q: Users keep typing instructions such as 'ignore all previous rules' to bypass a Bedrock assistant's behavior. Which Guardrails capability addresses this?

options.A: Word filters with a custom profanity list
options.B: Contextual grounding checks on responses
options.C: Content filters using prompt attack detection
options.D: Sensitive information filters for PII masking

why: Content filters include a prompt attack category that detects attempts to override the model's instructions.

others.t: Profanity word filters only catch listed words, not instruction-override phrasing.
Grounding checks verify answers against sources, not user instructions.
Sensitive information filters detect PII, not jailbreak attempts.

q: A legal team worries that generated content might resemble copyrighted training material and expose the company to liability. Which choice addresses the legal exposure itself?

options.A: Enable Guardrails sensitive information filters on outputs
options.B: Run SageMaker Clarify bias analysis on every prompt
options.C: Add Amazon A2I human review to every generated output
options.D: Choose a model provider that offers IP indemnification

why: IP indemnification is a contractual protection that shifts infringement legal risk away from the customer.

others.t: Sensitive information filters handle PII, not copyright liability.
Clarify measures bias and explainability, not copyright.
Human review might catch some content but does not transfer legal liability.

q: A company wants to discover which Amazon S3 buckets contain stored personal data before using the files as training data. Which service fits?

options.A: Amazon A2I
options.B: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock
options.C: SageMaker Model Cards
options.D: Amazon Macie

why: Macie discovers and classifies sensitive data, including PII, stored in S3.

others.t: A2I provides human review of predictions, not data discovery.
Guardrails redacts PII in live prompts and responses, not stored buckets.
Model Cards document models and do not scan data.

q: Which action is the MOST direct way to reduce the environmental footprint of adding generative AI to an application?

options.A: Add Guardrails content filters to every request
options.B: Reuse a pretrained foundation model with prompting or RAG
options.C: Publish an AI Service Card for the application
options.D: Train a new foundation model from scratch for exclusivity

why: Reusing a pretrained model avoids the large compute and energy cost of training from scratch.

others.t: Content filters address safety, not energy use.
An AI Service Card is documentation and does not change energy use.
Training from scratch consumes the most compute and energy.

q: A colleague says 'our model has high variance, so it is biased against women.' What is wrong with this statement?

options.A: Variance measures dataset size, which is unrelated to fairness
options.B: Nothing; high variance is a recognized type of fairness bias
options.C: Bias and variance are two names for one fairness measurement
options.D: Variance describes sensitivity to training data, not unfair treatment

why: Variance is a model-sensitivity concept (overfitting). Fairness bias is about inequitable treatment of groups, so the two should not be conflated.

others.t: Variance is not a measure of dataset size.
High variance does not by itself imply unfair treatment of any group.
Bias (unfair outcomes for groups) and variance (sensitivity to training data) are different concepts, not synonyms.

q: A model passes a Clarify fairness report with no gaps across gender and age groups. Yet it performs poorly for customers in one new region that is nearly absent from training data. What explains the clean report?

options.A: Representativeness bias; the region was never a facet
options.B: Clarify only supports age and gender attributes by design
options.C: Historical bias inside the fairness metric calculations
options.D: Label bias from annotators who work in that region

why: When a whole segment is thin in the data and no group label exists for it, group-based fairness metrics cannot reveal it. Check per-segment coverage and accuracy separately.

others.t: Clarify works on facets you specify; the gap is that no region facet or coverage was checked.
Historical bias is about an inequitable real world reflected in data, not a missing segment.
Nothing in the stem points to annotator labeling issues.

q: A health model uses one set of thresholds for every patient, but diabetes markers behave differently across ethnic groups, causing worse accuracy for some. Which bias is this?

options.A: Aggregation bias in the model design
options.B: Sampling bias in the patient data
options.C: Exclusion bias in the feature set
options.D: Label bias in the clinical labels

why: Aggregation bias is applying one model uniformly to groups that need distinct treatment.

others.t: Sampling bias is about the data not representing the population; the stem is about uniform treatment.
Exclusion bias means relevant features or data were dropped, which is not described.
Label bias comes from annotators, and none are mentioned.

q: A hospital wants to check whether its trained triage model misses disease more often in one demographic group. Which Clarify post-training metric is the best match?

options.A: Class imbalance
options.B: Accuracy or recall difference
options.C: Contextual grounding score
options.D: Difference in proportions of labels

why: Accuracy and recall difference compares how well the trained model performs across groups, which is what healthcare triage needs.

others.t: Class imbalance is a pre-training dataset metric.
Grounding checks belong to Guardrails and apply to generative output.
DPL is a pre-training dataset label metric.

q: A team improves fairness for a hiring model by adjusting decision thresholds per group after training, losing a little overall accuracy. Which fairness-mitigation stage is this?

options.A: Post-processing after model training
options.B: In-processing during model training
options.C: Data labeling before model training
options.D: Pre-processing before model training

why: Adjusting thresholds after the model is trained is post-processing threshold calibration.

others.t: In-processing adds fairness constraints during training.
Labeling is data preparation and does not adjust thresholds.
Pre-processing changes the data, such as rebalancing, before training.

q: For which use case is accepting lower accuracy in exchange for interpretability MOST justified?

options.A: Spam filtering for a personal email inbox
options.B: Tagging holiday photos in a photo album
options.C: Loan approvals under regulatory review
options.D: Ranking music playlists for daily listening

why: High-stakes regulated decisions such as credit require explanations, so interpretability can outweigh a small accuracy gain.

others.t: Spam errors are low-stakes and easily corrected.
Photo tagging is low-stakes and unregulated.
Playlist ranking is low-stakes and has no explanation requirement.

q: A team needs thousands of images labeled by human annotators to train a classifier, and wants consistent labeling workflows. Which service fits?

options.A: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Clarify
options.C: Amazon SageMaker Ground Truth
options.D: Amazon SageMaker Model Cards

why: SageMaker Ground Truth manages human data labeling for training datasets.

others.t: Guardrails filters live foundation-model traffic.
Clarify detects bias and explains predictions; it does not label data.
Model Cards document models, not label data.

q: Which statement about SageMaker Clarify and Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock is correct?

options.A: Clarify covers datasets and models; Guardrails filters live FM traffic
options.B: Clarify filters and blocks harmful live foundation-model responses
options.C: Guardrails computes SHAP feature attributions for tabular models
options.D: Both tools only analyze data before a model is deployed

why: Clarify handles bias and explainability for datasets and trained models; Guardrails applies runtime safety and privacy filters on foundation-model traffic.

others.t: Live output filtering is Guardrails' job.
SHAP explainability belongs to Clarify.
Guardrails works at inference time, not on training data.

q: A system has a tabular approval model plus a Bedrock assistant that writes the customer letter. How should responsible AI tooling be assigned?

options.A: Only Clarify on both, reported as one blended metric
options.B: Guardrails on the tabular model and Clarify on the assistant
options.C: Only Model Cards for both, with no runtime tooling or monitoring
options.D: Clarify on the tabular model, Guardrails on the assistant

why: Clarify fits the structured model's bias and explainability, and Guardrails fits the generative component, each monitored independently.

others.t: Clarify does not filter live FM output, and blended metrics hide per-component problems.
This reverses the tools' scopes.
A Model Card is documentation and does not provide runtime protection.

q: After deployment, a team wants alerts if a model's disparate impact worsens over months. Which pairing supports this?

options.A: Mechanical Turk together with Cognito
options.B: Amazon Macie together with Ground Truth
options.C: AI Service Cards together with Guardrails
options.D: Model Monitor together with Clarify

why: Clarify integrates with SageMaker Model Monitor to track bias drift on a deployed endpoint.

others.t: These are workforce and identity pieces, not monitoring.
Macie finds sensitive data in S3 and Ground Truth labels data; neither tracks bias drift.
AI Service Cards are static documentation and Guardrails filters content.

q: Which design BEST demonstrates the controllability dimension of responsible AI?

options.A: Using SHAP values to describe feature influence on each prediction
options.B: Removing a proxy feature from the training dataset
options.C: Publishing a card describing training data sources
options.D: Letting a human reviewer override low-confidence predictions

why: Controllability means a human can monitor, override or stop the system, which A2I human review enables.

others.t: SHAP supports explainability.
Removing a proxy feature supports fairness.
Documentation of training data supports transparency.

q: A company deploys a customer-facing Bedrock assistant and must stop it from producing hateful or offensive text. Which TWO Guardrails features directly block that kind of output? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Content filters for hate, insults and violence
options.B: Word filters that block profanity
options.C: Contextual grounding checks against source documents
options.D: Sensitive information filters that mask account numbers

why: Content filters block harmful categories such as hate, insults and violence, and word filters block listed offensive words or phrases. Both stop harmful text at runtime, which is the safety dimension.

others.t: Grounding checks verify answers against source content, which targets made-up facts rather than offensive text.
Sensitive information filters detect and mask personal data, which is a privacy control rather than a harmful-language control.

q: A team is filling in a SageMaker Model Card for its own custom model. Which TWO items belong in it? (Select TWO.)

options.A: A public Mechanical Turk workforce definition
options.B: A runtime filter that redacts PII from prompts
options.C: Evaluation metrics and training data description
options.D: Intended use and known limitations

why: A Model Card is structured documentation of a model you built: intended use, limitations, training data and evaluation results.

others.t: Workforce definitions belong to labeling or A2I setup, not model documentation.
PII redaction at runtime is a Guardrails configuration, not Model Card content.

q: A team has only a dataset and no trained model yet. Which TWO Clarify metrics can they compute? (Select TWO.)

options.A: Disparate impact
options.B: Class imbalance
options.C: Accuracy difference
options.D: Difference in proportions of labels

why: Class imbalance and DPL are computed on the raw dataset before training.

others.t: Disparate impact needs a trained model's predictions.
Accuracy difference compares a trained model's performance across groups.

q: Which of the following is NOT a capability of Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: Denied topics that block restricted subjects
options.B: Contextual grounding checks on responses
options.C: Word filters for custom blocked phrases
options.D: Generating SHAP feature attributions

why: SHAP attributions come from SageMaker Clarify. Guardrails filters foundation-model input and output at runtime.

others.t: Denied topics is a real Guardrails capability.
Contextual grounding checks are a real Guardrails capability.
Word filters are a real Guardrails capability.
